claims.text: Baseline MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration material is typically brittle.
Baseline MnNiSi-based material has a large magnetocaloric effect under standard synthesis conditions.
Replacing approximately 5 atomic% Ni with Co improves mechanical performance.
Approximately 5 atomic% Co substitution retains the large magnetocaloric effect of the parent material.
Co segregates to grain boundaries in the modified MnNiSi-based alloy.
Co substitution enhances grain-boundary cohesion and intergranular bonding.
Co substitution may refine the alloy microstructure.
The Co-induced microstructural modification does not dramatically alter the magnetostructural transition.
Co changes the local chemistry at grain boundaries.
The proposed Co-induced microstructure facilitates dislocation motion and thereby increases ductility or toughness.
The magnetic ordering responsible for the magnetocaloric effect is preserved after low-level Co substitution.
At approximately 5 atomic% Co, fracture toughness increases significantly relative to the undoped baseline.
At approximately 5 atomic% Co, tensile strength increases significantly relative to the undoped baseline.
At approximately 5 atomic% Co, adiabatic temperature change and isothermal entropy change remain within approximately 10% of the undoped baseline values.
The hypothesized benefit holds for Co substitutions up to about 5 atomic%.
Co additions above about 5 atomic% may cause mechanical and magnetic properties to deviate from the desired behavior.

contradictions.description: The phrase '5 atomic% of Ni' can mean replacement of 5% of the Ni sublattice, whereas '5 atomic% Co doping' denotes Co as 5% of all atoms. These correspond to different compositions for nominal MnNiSi and should be disambiguated.
